chemicals.name: Water
chemicals.description: Distilled water. The universal solvent. Used to dilute acids and bases - but ALWAYS add acid to water, never water to acid.

chemicals.name: Hydrochloric Acid
chemicals.description: A strong acid that fumes in air. Reacts with bases to form salt and water, and with metals to release hydrogen gas.

chemicals.name: Sodium Hydroxide
chemicals.description: A strong base, also called caustic soda. Dissolving it in water releases heat. Neutralises acids.

chemicals.name: Sulfuric Acid
chemicals.description: A dense, oily strong acid. Its heat of dilution is violent - adding water to concentrated sulfuric acid can make it boil and spit.

chemicals.name: Copper(II) Sulfate
chemicals.description: Bright blue salt solution. Reacts with sodium hydroxide to form a pale blue precipitate of copper hydroxide.

chemicals.name: Potassium Permanganate
chemicals.description: A deep purple oxidising agent. Its colour fades as it is reduced, which makes it a useful visual indicator.

chemicals.name: Ethanol
chemicals.description: A volatile, flammable alcohol. Burns with a pale blue flame. Keep away from open burners.

chemicals.name: Sodium Chloride
chemicals.description: Common table salt. Dissolves readily in water to give a clear, neutral solution.

chemicals.name: Acetone
chemicals.description: A fast-evaporating solvent used to clean glassware. Highly flammable vapour.

chemicals.name: Dilute Sulfuric Acid
chemicals.description: Sulfuric acid diluted in water. Still corrosive, but far less aggressive than the concentrated form.

chemicals.name: Salt Water
chemicals.description: The neutral product of an acid-base reaction, or simply salt dissolved in water.

chemicals.name: Copper(II) Hydroxide
chemicals.description: A pale blue gelatinous precipitate. Formed when a base meets a copper salt solution.

chemicals.name: Unknown Mixture
chemicals.description: Two substances with no known reaction between them. They have simply mixed.

warning.title: NEVER add water to concentrated acid!
warning.text: Dilution releases intense heat right at the surface. The water can flash-boil and spit concentrated acid out of the beaker and into your face. Correct procedure: add the ACID to the WATER, slowly, down the side of the vessel, while stirring.

result.note: Acid has splattered - the bench needs cleaning.

warning.title: Correct procedure: acid into water
warning.text: The large volume of water absorbs the heat of dilution safely. The mixture only becomes warm. This is always the right order when diluting a concentrated acid.

result.note: Safely diluted acid, warm to the touch.

warning.title: Neutralisation
warning.text: A strong acid plus a strong base gives a neutral salt solution and water: HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O. The reaction is exothermic, so the beaker feels warm.

warning.title: Precipitation
warning.text: Sodium hydroxide meets copper(II) sulfate and an insoluble pale blue solid, copper(II) hydroxide, drops out of the clear blue solution.

result.note: A pale blue precipitate has formed.
The purple colour has been discharged by oxidation.

warning.title: Oxidiser plus flammable solvent!
warning.text: A strong oxidising agent and a volatile flammable solvent can ignite on contact. Never store or mix oxidisers with solvents; keep them on separate shelves.

result.note: Burnt residue - use the fire extinguisher next time.
